newsitem.title: SPAIN: Basque ETA separatists free two hostages.
newsitem.headline: Basque ETA separatists free two hostages.

text.p: Two hostages held by the Basque guerrilla group ETA were freed on Tuesday, and Spanish police arrested four suspected separatist rebels, officials said.
Basque businessman Cosme Delclaux, an ETA prisoner for the past 232 days, was found drugged and tied to a tree near Bilbao.
His family had paid his captors $6.85 million, the largest ransom obtained by ETA, and agreed in secret negotiations to pay a further $3.4 million after his release, police sources said.
Only hours later, the civil guard found ETA's longest-held captive, prison worker Jose Antonio Ortega Lara, in a tiny cell beneath a warehouse near the Basque town of Mondragon.
As part of the same operation, police arrested four suspected ETA rebels in different locations throughout the province, who were believed to have taken turns in guarding the prisoners.

"We are very satisfied, not only as the government but as Spaniards," government spokesman Miguel Angel Rodriguez said. "We see that two people who have been tormented are not being tormented anymore".

ETA, which stands for Basque Homeland and Freedom, has waged a 29-year struggle for independence from Spain in which 800 people have been killed. The group has kidnapped 76 people since 1970, of whom 68 survived the ordeal.
The rebels also collect a "revolutionary tax" from businessmen in the Basque region under threat of violence.
Authorities said Delclaux, 34, was released just after midnight following an anonymous phone call to a newspaper with links to ETA.

He was found tied to a tree about 25 km (15 miles) from Bilbao, near the town of Elorrio in the Basque province of Vizcaya. Officials said he was disoriented, apparently as a result of being given some type of sedative, but was in good health.
Police later freed Ortega Lara, who had been held captive for 532 days. He was found in an abandoned industrial area near Mondragon.
Police had to untangle a sophisticated hydraulic system to access his cell which took almost two hours, Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja said.
Mayor Oreja said police had located the general area where Ortega Lara was being held some weeks ago, but only homed in on the industrial site in the last day.
"This was probably a site where other prisoners were held in the past," he said.
Ortega Lara appeared in good health but was taken to a hospital in San Sebastian for an examination.

He was abducted from the northern Spanish town of Burgos on January 17, 1996. ETA said it kidnapped him to put pressure on the government to end what it termed the repression of Basque political prisoners.
Delclaux, a lawyer and the son of a wealthy Basque industrialist, was kidnapped on his way home from work as a consultant at a multimedia firm in a Vizcaya technological park on November 11, 1996.
In recent weeks, his family was reported to have received a package containing two bullets, interpreted as a threat to execute him unless payment was made.
